static_review.evidence: Compared zil-syntax lexer quoted/escape with zil-types utf8_literals::decode. Both admit n/r/t/0/backslash/single-quote/double-quote escapes; Unicode escapes require 1 through 6 ASCII hex digits and a valid Unicode scalar. Surrogates, overlong hex, missing braces, unknown escapes, unescaped quote and physical CR/LF reject. Direct UTF8 scalars, NUL and combining sequences preserve exact bytes without normalization.

Ordinary CoreExprKind::String reaches a dedicated runtime producer without matching function names. The producer revalidates spelling rather than trusting lexer provenance; raw Core examples cover missing delimiters, invalid scalar and unsupported escape. Both inference paths and known-type lookup preserve immutable Address<Slice<U8>>. Actual production rejects mutable expected types through existing complete type equality. Unreachable statements remain fail-closed in the existing Builder.

utf8_literal prepays twice the spelling length before either allocation-free decode pass. The first pass computes exact decoded UTF8 length; length plus six type nodes is charged before Vec::with_capacity, byte filling and two Address/Slice/U8 trees. No output terminator or implicit owner is introduced. Runtime StaticUtf8 is explicitly forbidden in CT evaluation. Existing Source-byte and Types work-boundary tests are present but were not executed by this reviewer.
